results.title: Joliet Resource Lookup
results.description:
Overview

This feature service provides a municipal reference dataset for the City of Joliet and surrounding communities. It brings together foundational boundary, address, parcel, and public-service layers used to support address lookup, jurisdictional reference, planning, and map display.

Feature Layers
  • Master Address Location – Point-based master address records with address status, type, use, municipality, postal and ZIP code, unit information, and related parcel and street references.
  • Neighborhood – Neighborhood boundaries with housing and acreage attributes for Joliet neighborhood planning and reporting.
  • Subdivision – City subdivision boundaries used to identify named subdivision areas and related administrative tracking.
  • Zip Code – ZIP code boundary layer for Joliet and nearby communities.
  • Library District, Council District, and Park District – Local government and service district boundaries for civic reference and jurisdictional lookup.
  • Township – Township boundaries and township-range reference information.
  • Elementary School District and High School District – School district boundaries for educational service areas.
  • Historic Property – Historic property records linked to historic districts and parcel identifiers, supporting preservation and planning workflows.
  • FIRM 2019 – Flood Insurance Rate Map coverage showing flood hazard zones and related floodplain attributes.
  • Zoning – City zoning boundaries and classifications, including zoning status, ordinance history, special uses, conditional uses, and planned development information.
  • City Boundary – Boundary of Joliet and neighboring communities for regional context.
  • Building – Building footprint layer for the City of Joliet with building type, name, size, year built, stories, and related source metadata.
  • Parcel – Parcel polygons with ownership and mailing information, land and building values, address links, and parcel status details.
Geographic Coverage

The service covers the City of Joliet, Illinois, and surrounding areas in Will, Kendall, Grundy, and LaSalle counties. It supports both citywide and regional reference use across local jurisdictions.

Use Cases
  • Address search and location lookup
  • Jurisdiction and service-area reference
  • Land use, zoning, and parcel research
  • Public safety, emergency response, and civic planning support
  • Boundary display for neighborhoods, districts, school areas, and townships
  • Floodplain and historic preservation review
  • Building inventory and property analysis
results.snippet: A municipal reference service for Joliet, Illinois, featuring address locations, parcels, zoning, district boundaries, buildings, and related planning and lookup layers.

results.name: Industrial
results.title: Industrial
results.description: This file is a digital geospatial Environmental Systems Research Institute (ESRI) ArcGIS version 10.x File Geodatabase Polygon Feature Class representing land use in the seven northeastern Illinois counties (Cook, DuPage, Kane, Kendall, Lake, McHenry and Will). Land use is identified to nearly 60 categories, and was created using county parcel GIS boundaries and Assessor data, along with color orthorectificed aerial photography captured in the spring of 2015. Land uses were assigned to parcels using a combination of automated and manual techniques, using a variety of reference data sets for land use identification and validation. Parcels were then dissolved on common land uses (to the limits of PLS sections or assessor blocks); polygons were generated for “non-parcel” (water, right-of-way) areas and classified using automated processes, and extensive topological cleaning was necessary to minimize gap/overlap issues.NOTE: Land use polygons are based on county parcel boundaries; special care must be exercised when comparing these data to earlier (2005, 2001, 1990) Inventories, which relied on manual drafting of land use boundaries that would extend to road centerlines.
results.snippet: The Land Use Inventory for Northeastern Illinois is produced by the Chicago Metropolitan Agency for Planning (CMAP). Identification of land use in the seven-county region of northeast Illinois serves in CMAP's development of long-range population, household and employment forecasts in support of the comprehensive planning efforts. Additionally, agency planners and analysts frequently use Inventory for local technical assistance, watershed planning, and policy analyses. Counties, municipalities, transportation agencies, universities, developers, and conservation groups also make use of these data.
results.accessInformation: CMAP Research and Analysis staff: David Clark (P.M.), Erik Pedersen, Noel Peterson.  Interns: Kyle Acevedo, Damilare Balogun, Jeong Hoon Kim, Roxanna Lewicki.
results.licenseInfo: It is required that the Chicago Metropolitan Agency for Planning be cited in any products generated from the data. The following source citation must be included: "Source: Chicago Metropolitan Agency for Planning's 2015 Land Use Inventory for Northeastern Illinois, Version 1.0. Published: November 2020." Map information is not appropriate for, and is not to be used as, a geodetic, legal, or engineering base. Map information has no legal basis in the definition of boundaries or property lines and is not intended as a substitute for surveyed locations such as can be determined by a registered Public Land Surveyor.

results.name: CMAP_Land_Use_Inventory__2020
results.title: CMAP_Land_Use_Inventory__2020
results.description:
This file is a digital geospatial Environmental Systems Research Institute (ESRI) ArcGIS version 10.x File Geodatabase Polygon Feature Class representing land use in the seven northeastern Illinois counties (Cook, DuPage, Kane, Kendall, Lake, McHenry and Will). Land use is identified to nearly 60 categories and was created using county parcel GIS boundaries and Assessor data, along with color orthorectificed aerial photography captured in the spring of YEAR. Land uses were assigned to parcels using a combination of automated and manual techniques, using a variety of reference data sets for land use identification and validation. Parcels were then dissolved on common land uses (to the limits of PLS sections or assessor blocks); polygons were generated for “non-parcel” (water, right-of-way) areas and classified using automated processes, and have been assigned a generic code of 6000 (non-parcel).

NOTES:

Land use polygons are based on county parcel geometry; special care must be exercised when comparing these data to earlier (2005, 2001, 1990) Inventories, which relied on manual drafting of land use boundaries that would extend to road centerlines.

Parcel geometry received from the counties is used “as-is,” meaning there was no attempt to reconcile sliver gaps or overlaps between polygons in a county’s parcel set, nor along county boundaries where parcels may overlap slightly.

Values for the landuse and open space management fields are coded domains. See tables domain_LANDUSE and domain_OSMGMT for code descriptions. Full description of land use categories can be found in the accompanying Land Use Classification Scheme PDF document.

Additionally, agency planners and analysts frequently use Inventory for local technical assistance, watershed planning, and policy analyses. Counties, municipalities, transportation agencies, universities, developers, and conservation groups also make use of these data.

results.title: RCUP Public Datasets
results.description:
This public GIS database was created as the geospatial supplement to the 2021 Joint Base San Antonio (JBSA) Regional Compatible Use Plan, facilitated by the Alamo Area Council of Governments (AACOG).

The AACOG Compatible Use Program facilitates communication and collaboration between local Joint Base San Antonio military installations and municipal, county and community stakeholders.  The Compatible Use Program promotes compatible civilian development and activities in support of the local military mission; preserves and protects the public health, safety, and general welfare; enhances the security of installation missions; protects and preserves military readiness and quality of life; and enhances civilian, and military communications, and collaboration.

The Compatible Use Program is made possible through the support of the U.S. Department of Defense Office of Local Defense Community Cooperation (OLDCC) and AACOG members.
